mainTopic: A creditor takes one brother's share after an inheritance is divided; and how to value property when appraisers disagree
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier comparison: the grain-sale rule is a special rule of the רבנן made to suit both buyer and seller, so it cannot teach us about dividing property. Then the גמרא brings a new מחלוקת. Brothers divided their father's estate, and later the father's בעל חוב took one brother's share. רב says the division is void, because the brothers are still יורשין (heirs). שמואל says that brother gave up his claim, because the brothers are like לקוחות (buyers) without אחריות (a guarantee). רב אסי is unsure which is right, so the brother takes a quarter in land and a quarter in money. רב פפא rules that the brothers each give up a bit so all end up equal. אמימר rules the division is void, and the final הלכה follows him. Next, a ברייתא teaches about three appraisers who disagree on a property's value: the majority wins, and when all three differ there are three opinions (100, 90, or dividing the gap into thirds). The גמרא explains that the 100 view takes the middle estimate, and it starts explaining the 90 view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the grain-sale case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier comparison. In the grain-sale case, the רבנן made a rule that suits both the seller and the buyer, so that case cannot be compared to dividing property.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, in the grain sale, the רבנן made a rule that works well for the seller and also works well for the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a comparison raised just before this. It explains why the grain-sale case cannot teach us anything about brothers dividing property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in the grain sale was not based on pure logic about ownership. It was a תקנה (special rule) of the רבנן, made because it benefits both sides. A special rule like that cannot be stretched to cover a different case, like a division of property.

keyTerms.meaning: It suits him / is good for him

phrases.english: There, the Sages instituted a matter
phrases.notes: "There" means the grain-sale case the גמרא was just comparing to.

phrases.english: that is suitable for the seller

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a comparison raised before this section began.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: one is a special rule of the רבנן made for both sides' benefit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the grain-sale rule shows how any division or sale works.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grain-sale rule is a special תקנה made for both parties' benefit, so it cannot be applied to other cases.

steps.title: Three opinions on a creditor who takes one brother's share
steps.stepSummary: Brothers divided an inheritance, and then the father's creditor took one brother's share. רב says the division is void. שמואל says that brother gave up his claim. רב אסי says he takes a quarter in land and a quarter in money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Brothers divided their father's estate. Then a creditor came and took one brother's portion. רב says: the division is cancelled. שמואל says: that brother gave up his claim. רב אסי says: he takes a quarter in land and a quarter in money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a מחלוקת among אמוראים. Two brothers split an inheritance, and then a creditor takes one brother's share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב, the brothers start over and split whatever is left. Under שמואל, the brother who lost his share has no claim against the other brother. רב אסי takes a middle path: the brother gets something back, half in land and half in money.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute among אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: Here מַחְלוֹקֶת does not mean a dispute. It means the division of the property between the brothers.

phrases.english: It was stated: Brothers who divided [their inheritance],
and took the portion of one of them;
phrases.notes: This is a creditor of the father, collecting the father's debt from the land.

phrases.english: Rav says: The division is void.
And Shmuel says: He has given up [his claim].
He takes a quarter in land

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about dividing property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the division is void. שמואל: the brother waived his claim. רב אסי: he takes a quarter in land and a quarter in money.

steps.title: רב's reasoning: the brothers are still heirs
steps.stepSummary: רב says the division is void because he holds that brothers who divided an estate are still יורשין (heirs).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says the division is void, because he holds that brothers who divided are heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the thinking behind רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brothers are still considered heirs even after dividing, the father's debt belongs to all of them together. So when the creditor takes one share, it is as if the debt was paid for everyone. The remaining property must then be divided again.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he is of the opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole מחלוקת depends on one question: after dividing, are the brothers still heirs, or are they like buyers from each other?

phrases.english: Rav says: The division is void –

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בָּטְלָה מַחְלוֹקֶת – קָא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב's opinion from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who divided an estate are still considered heirs, so the division is undone when a creditor takes one share.

steps.title: שמואל's reasoning: the brothers are like buyers without a guarantee
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the brother gave up his claim because brothers who divided are like לקוחות (buyers) from each other, and like a buyer without אחריות (a guarantee).
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says the brother gave up his claim, because he holds that brothers who divided are like buyers, and like a buyer who bought without a guarantee.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the thinking behind שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל sees the division as if each brother bought his share from the other. A buyer without a guarantee cannot go back to the seller if a creditor takes the field. So the brother who lost his share has no claim against his brother.

keyTerms.meaning: Without a guarantee (against loss from a creditor)
Is similar to / is considered like

steps.whatToRemember: רב: after dividing, the brothers are still heirs, so the division is undone. שמואל: they are like buyers without a guarantee, so the brother who lost his share has no claim.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: He has given up –
and are like a purchaser without a guarantee.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains שמואל's opinion, the opposite of רב's reasoning in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who divided are like buyers without a guarantee, so the one whose share was taken has no claim against the other.

steps.title: Why רב אסי splits the payment between land and money
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי is unsure whether brothers who divided are heirs or buyers. So he splits the brother's claim: a quarter in land, as an heir would get, and a quarter in money, as a buyer would get.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי is unsure whether the brothers count as heirs or as buyers. So the brother takes a quarter in land and a quarter in money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רב אסי's ruling from Step 2. It completes the list of reasons after רב (Step 3) and שמואל (Step 4).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי is unsure whether the brothers are still יורשין or whether they are לקוחות. Here 'buyers' means buyers who are paid back for their loss, not שמואל's buyers without a guarantee, who get nothing. So he gives half of the brother's claim the way an heir is paid, in land, and half the way a buyer with a guarantee is paid, in money.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt; he is unsure

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'buyer' side means a buyer who is paid back in money. That is why the second quarter is paid in money and not in land.

phrases.english: therefore he takes a quarter in land

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the series of explanations for the three opinions in Step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the doubt whether brothers are heirs or buyers, the brother receives a quarter in land and a quarter in money.

steps.title: רב פפא's ruling: the brothers share the loss
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that in all these cases the brothers each give up part of their share. That way the brother who lost his portion ends up equal with the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the הלכה in all these teachings is that they take off a share from their portions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a practical ruling for all the cases in this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not cancel the division. Instead, each brother who still has his portion hands over some of it to the brother who lost his. In the end everyone has an equal share.

keyTerms.meaning: They take off a share; each gives a little from his portion

phrases.english: the halakha in all these teachings is

phrases.notes: Each brother who still has land gives a bit of his portion to the brother who lost his, so all end up equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכְתָא בְּכׇל הָנֵי שְׁמַעְתָּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the opinions to deciding the practical הלכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The brothers each give part of their portion so all are equal.

steps.title: אמימר's ruling: the division is canceled
steps.stepSummary: אמימר disagrees with רב פפא and rules that the original division is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: the division is void.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר offers a different practical ruling: the brothers' division is canceled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רב's view from Step 2, that the division is void because the brothers are still heirs. So the whole estate is divided again from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the division of the property, not a dispute

steps.confusionAlert: Here מחלוקת does not mean an argument. It means the brothers' division of the property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The division is void, following רב.

steps.title: Final ruling: the division is void
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the הלכה follows אמימר: the division is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: the division is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling, siding with אמימר and רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Between the two rulings, the גמרא chooses אמימר's. So when a creditor takes one brother's portion, the brothers divide the estate again from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: if the father's creditor takes one brother's share after the division, the division is void and the brothers divide again, like רב.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: the division is void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב פפא and אמימר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אמימר and רב: the division is void.

steps.title: Three appraisers: the majority wins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when three appraisers disagree and two of them agree, the single appraiser's estimate is canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: three people went to appraise a property. If one says 100 and two say 200, or one says 200 and two say 100, the single person is outvoted by the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא about appraisers who disagree about a property's value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two of the three appraisers agree, it does not matter whether the lone opinion is higher or lower. The majority's estimate is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: To appraise; to estimate the value
The single opinion is canceled because it is the minority

phrases.english: three who went down to appraise
one says it is worth a maneh,
the single one is nullified in his minority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, after the inheritance discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two appraisers agree, the third appraiser's estimate is canceled.

steps.title: Three different estimates: the property is valued at 100
steps.stepSummary: When all three appraisers give different estimates (100 דינרים, 20 סלעים, 30 סלעים), the first opinion in the ברייתא says the property is valued at 100.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says 100, another says 20, and another says 30, it is valued at 100.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a harder case where no two appraisers agree. It gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty and thirty here are counted in סלעים, which are 80 and 120 דינרים. The middle point of the three estimates is 100, so the property is valued at 100.

keyTerms.meaning: It is judged; it is valued at

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 20 and 30 as דינרים. They are סלעים (80 and 120 דינרים), so they are close to 100.

phrases.english: one says it is worth a maneh,
it is assessed at a maneh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּמָנֶה, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּעֶשְׂרִים, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a case where no two appraisers agree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With estimates of 80, 100, and 120 דינרים, the property is valued at 100.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק: the property is valued at 90
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק disagrees and says the property is valued at 90.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says: it is valued at ninety.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the ברייתא disagrees with the first opinion about the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He also looks at the three estimates, but he ends up at 90, not 100. The ברייתא does not give his reason, but the גמרא starts to explain it in Step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר: נִדּוֹן בְּתִשְׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in Step 10

steps.title: אחרים: measure the gap and divide it by three
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say to take the gap between the estimates and divide it into thirds.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: they make an appraisal between them and divide it into three.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא gives yet another way to settle the disagreement among the appraisers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים look at the space between the highest and lowest estimates and divide that gap into thirds. This is a third method, different from both 100 and 90.

keyTerms.meaning: "Others": a תנא quoted without his name

phrases.english: they make an appraisal between them,
phrases.notes: They measure the gap between the highest and lowest estimates.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: עוֹשִׂין שׁוּמָא בֵּינֵיהֶן, וּמְשַׁלְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third opinion on the same case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Take the gap between the estimates and divide it into thirds.

steps.title: The first opinion follows the middle estimate
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the opinion valuing the property at a מנה is choosing the middle estimate between the two extremes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the property is valued at a מנה (100) is going with the middle estimate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first opinion of the ברייתא from Step 10 and explains why it says 100.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three estimates were 80 (20 סלעים), 100, and 120 (30 סלעים). The estimate of 100 sits exactly in the middle, so this opinion simply takes the middle appraiser's number.

keyTerms.meaning: It is judged / valued (the property is assessed at)
The middle matter, the middle estimate

steps.confusionAlert: The estimates are given in different coins. A סלע equals 4 דינרים, so 20 סלעים is 80 and 30 סלעים is 120. Once you convert them, 100 is clearly the middle.

phrases.english: The one who says it is valued at a maneh

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the first opinion quoted in Step 10, after the ברייתא's three opinions were listed in Steps 10-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion values the property at 100 because it takes the middle of the three estimates.

steps.title: Starting to explain why רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says 90
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's valuation of 90, starting with how he views the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק says it is valued at 90, because he holds that this land...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second opinion from Step 11 and starts to give its reason. The sentence is not finished here, so this line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 90 is not the middle estimate, so רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק must be reasoning differently from the first opinion. The words "he holds that this land" introduce his view of what the land is really worth, and the full reason follows in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he is of the opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
because he holds that this land...

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר נִדּוֹן בְּתִשְׁעִים קָא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first opinion's reasoning, the גמרא moves on to explain the second opinion, רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק's valuation of 90 is based on his view of the land's worth. The explanation continues past this point.
